title: Founder case: Craigslist grows from an email list

sources.claim: Craig Newmark began emailing San Francisco event notices to friends in 1995; people asked to join and started posting other things such as jobs and apartments; the list moved to the web and was incorporated as a company in 1999.

sections.skill: Apply a documented early decision: grow a useful list around what people ask for

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did it start?

choices.text: A paid newspaper with printed classified ads
A television show about San Francisco local events
An email list of local event notices for friends

questions.correct_answer: An email list of local event notices for friends
questions.intro: Documented history (Encyclopedia.com): Craig Newmark began emailing San Francisco event notices to friends in 1995. People asked to join, and they started posting other things such as jobs and apartments. The list moved to the web and was incorporated as a company in 1999. Lesson drawn by this course (an interpretation): start by sharing something useful with people who asked for it, listen to what they start using it for, and grow the format around their needs. One success story does not guarantee the same result for another business.

questions.intro: Imagine pinning a sheet of local events on a café bulletin board. Soon neighbors add notes about lost pets, rooms for rent and jobs. You notice and add sections for each.
